summary: The lecture covers prehistoric Indian culture and human evolution stages (Miocene, Pliocene, Pleistocene). It details Paleolithic (Lower, Middle, Upper), Mesolithic, Neolithic, and Chalcolithic ages with their characteristic tools, sites, and cultural developments such as agriculture, pottery, and metal use.
points: Human evolution classified into Miocene (apes), Pliocene (Homo erectus, continental drift), Pleistocene (Homo sapiens, Ice Age).
Lower Paleolithic (2M–50k BC): Tools – Chopper, Skinner, Digger.
Middle Paleolithic (50k–40k BC): Flakes used to sharpen principal tools.
Upper Paleolithic: Burin for fishing; first monochrome white paintings at Bhimbetka (Raisen, MP).
Mesolithic (9k–8k BC): Microliths; first domesticated animal – wild dog (Adamgarh, MP; world: Palestine).
Neolithic: Agriculture first; Mehrgarh (Pakistan) – mud-brick houses; pottery at Chopani Mando (UP); Burzahom (Kashmir) – master and dog buried together.
Chalcolithic: First metal copper; stone still used; sites in Jorwe, Malwa, Kayatha, Ahar, Gilund; burial: adults N–S, children E–W; copper objects with dead.

check.q: In which geological epoch did Homo sapiens first appear?
Which tool, developed in the Upper Paleolithic, was specifically used for fishing?
At which Neolithic site were a master and his dog buried in the same grave?
